name: Trial Mountain Circuit
description: A legendary GT circuit carved through the Sierra Nevada mountains. Trial Mountain's dramatic elevation changes, three tunnels, and blind crests create one of sim racing's most exhilarating challenges. The long uphill back straight rewards power, while the technical mountain section demands precision and bravery.

keyCorners.name: Tunnel Entry (T3)
keyCorners.description: Sharp right-hander into the first tunnel. Late braking rewards brave drivers but overshoot and the wall waits.

keyCorners.name: Mountain Hairpin (T7)
keyCorners.description: Tight left-hand hairpin at the circuit's highest point. Traction on exit is critical for the descent.

keyCorners.name: Ridge Chicane (T10-11)
keyCorners.description: Fast left-right flick along the mountain ridge. Carries massive speed if committed, punishes hesitation.

keyCorners.name: Valley Sweep (T14)
keyCorners.description: High-speed right-hander leading onto the main straight. Exit speed defines lap time.

carSuitability.reason: Lightweight chassis excels through technical mountain section. D'ornellas proved this dominance in Round 1.
Balanced AWD chassis handles elevation changes with composure. Strong traction on uphill exits.
Mid-engine grip advantage in technical sections. Good power for the long straight.
Raw power exploits the 1.3km straight, but heavy chassis struggles through mountain hairpins.
Nimble and lightweight. Rewards smooth inputs through flowing corners.
Power suits the straight but weight hurts in the tight mountain section.

name: WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca
description: The first real-world circuit ever featured in Gran Turismo. Laguna Seca's dramatic elevation changes, blind crests, and the iconic Corkscrew make it one of motorsport's most demanding tracks. Short but intense — every corner matters here.

keyCorners.name: Andretti Hairpin (T2)
keyCorners.description: Named after Mario Andretti. A 180-degree left-hander where late braking can gain positions but risks track limits.

keyCorners.name: The Corkscrew (T8-8A)
keyCorners.description: The most famous corner in motorsport. A blind, plunging left-right with an 18% elevation drop. Commit fully or lose everything.

keyCorners.name: Rainey Curve (T9)
keyCorners.description: Fast left-hander at the bottom of the Corkscrew descent. Carries huge speed and rewards total commitment.

carSuitability.reason: Lightest car on the grid. Perfect for Laguna's technical demands and elevation changes.
Naturally aspirated V8 response suits the constant direction changes.
Lightweight agility pays dividends on this tight, technical layout.
AWD traction helps through the Corkscrew but extra weight limits corner speed.
Heaviest car struggles on a track with no long straights to exploit power.
AWD confidence through blind crests helps, but mass is a disadvantage.

name: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
description: The greatest racing circuit in the world. Spa-Francorchamps combines fearsome speed with technical complexity across 7 kilometers of Belgian Ardennes forest. Legendary corners, dramatic elevation, and notoriously unpredictable weather make every lap an adventure.

keyCorners.name: La Source (T1)
keyCorners.description: Tight first-gear hairpin at the top of the hill. Exit speed sets up the charge down to Eau Rouge.

keyCorners.name: Eau Rouge / Raidillon (T3-4)
keyCorners.description: The most iconic corner complex in motorsport. A compression into a blind, uphill left-right taken flat in GT3 cars. Pure commitment.

keyCorners.name: Pouhon (T11)
keyCorners.description: Double-apex, high-speed left-hander through a dip. Demands trust in downforce and absolute courage.

keyCorners.name: Bus Stop (T18-19)
keyCorners.description: Tight chicane before the pit straight. Heavy braking zone and prime overtaking spot.

carSuitability.reason: 625 HP and stability through Eau Rouge. Power advantage on Kemmel Straight is massive.
645 HP V10 dominates the long straights. If the driver can manage the weight through Bus Stop.
Balanced chassis handles everything Spa throws at it. AWD helps in wet conditions.
Lightweight but only 370 HP — gets eaten alive on Kemmel Straight.
AWD is a huge advantage in Spa's unpredictable weather. Strong through Eau Rouge.
550 HP and excellent stability. Well-suited to Spa's mix of speed and technicality.

name: Red Bull Ring
description: A short, explosive circuit set in the stunning Styrian mountains. With only 10 corners, every single turn matters immensely. Long straights connected by heavy braking zones create a pure racing spectacle with constant overtaking action.

keyCorners.name: Niki Lauda Kurve (T1)
keyCorners.description: 90-degree right-hander after the long pit straight. Prime overtaking zone with heavy braking from top speed.

keyCorners.name: Remus (T3)
keyCorners.description: Sweeping right-hander uphill. Carries good speed and sets up the approach to Turn 4.

keyCorners.name: Rauch (T4)
keyCorners.description: Blind right-hander over the crest. Full commitment required — the car gets light over the top.

keyCorners.name: Rindt Kurve (T7)
keyCorners.description: Fast right-hander leading onto the final straight. Exit speed defines overtaking potential.

carSuitability.reason: Maximum power for the 930m straight. Heavy braking suits the Viper's strong stoppers.
Power and braking stability make it ideal for stop-and-go circuits.
AWD traction on uphill exits and V10 power on straights.
370 HP is a death sentence on a 930m straight. Technical advantage doesn't apply with only 10 turns.
Good power-to-weight and responsive handling through the limited corner count.
Moderate power limits straight speed. Strong braking partially compensates.

name: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
description: Brazil's iconic racing cathedral. Interlagos runs counter-clockwise with a unique rhythm — the fast, flowing infield contrasts with technical braking zones and a long uphill main straight. Weather can change rapidly, adding drama to an already intense venue.

keyCorners.name: Senna S (T1-2)
keyCorners.description: Fast left-right esses named after Ayrton Senna. Downhill entry demands absolute precision — get it wrong and the whole lap suffers.

keyCorners.name: Descida do Lago (T4)
keyCorners.description: Long, descending left-hander. Rewards late braking and smooth inputs on the downhill approach.

keyCorners.name: Bico de Pato (T8)
keyCorners.description: Sharp left-hander that breaks the rhythm. Heavy braking from speed catches out the unwary.

keyCorners.name: Junção (T12)
keyCorners.description: Slow left-hander leading onto the long uphill main straight. Exit speed is critical — this corner defines lap time.

carSuitability.reason: Light weight excels through the flowing infield. D'ornellas's dominance continued here in Round 3.
Balanced chassis handles the mix of fast and slow corners. AWD helps in variable weather.
Hybrid power delivery suits the stop-and-go nature of the infield.
Good power-to-weight ratio and responsive handling through the technical infield.
AWD confidence in the Senna S helps, but weight penalty through the tight infield.
Power advantage on the main straight, but struggles through the tight Senna S complex.

name: Deep Forest Raceway
description: A classic GT circuit winding through dense Swiss forest. Deep Forest combines tight technical sections with flowing sweepers and atmospheric tunnel passages. The 18-corner layout demands complete versatility from both car and driver.

keyCorners.name: Forest Chicane (T3-4)
keyCorners.description: Tight left-right chicane through the tree line. Kerb riding is essential for maintaining speed.

keyCorners.name: Tunnel Section (T8-9)
keyCorners.description: Dark tunnel passage with a kink mid-way. Eyes need time to adjust — experienced drivers know the line by feel.

keyCorners.name: Lakeside Sweep (T13)
keyCorners.description: Long, fast right-hander along the lake edge. Carries massive speed if the entry angle is perfect.

keyCorners.name: Final Hairpin (T17)
keyCorners.description: Tight left-hander before the pit straight. Heavy braking and good traction needed for the run to the line.

carSuitability.reason: Lightweight chassis thrives through 18 corners. The less power you waste, the more you gain.
Neutral handling and braking stability are perfect for Deep Forest's technical demands.
Naturally aspirated V8 response suits the constant direction changes.
Lightweight and agile. The forest rewards finesse over power.
Heaviest car on a track with 18 corners and limited straight. A handful at best.
Mid-engine balance shines in technical, flowing sections.

name: Autopolis
description: A challenging Japanese circuit nestled in the mountains of Oita Prefecture. Autopolis combines long straights with tight technical sections, dramatic elevation changes, and notoriously changeable weather. The circuit's exposed hilltop location makes it especially punishing in wet conditions.

keyCorners.name: Turn 1 Hairpin
keyCorners.description: Tight right-hander at the end of the main straight. Prime overtaking opportunity with heavy braking from top speed.

keyCorners.name: Bridge Corner (T5-6)
keyCorners.description: Fast sweeping section over the bridge. Requires commitment and confidence in the car's aero grip.

keyCorners.name: Turn 10 Hairpin
keyCorners.description: Tight left-hand hairpin at the lowest point. Traction on exit is critical for the uphill run.

keyCorners.name: Final Chicane (T17-18)
keyCorners.description: Technical chicane before the main straight. Exit speed defines lap time.

carSuitability.reason: Lightweight chassis excels in the technical sections. Less exposed on the straight than at Red Bull Ring.
Power advantage on the 900m straight. Wet conditions add challenge but the V10 torque helps.
AWD traction is a massive advantage in Autopolis's wet conditions. Strong through technical sections.
Balanced chassis handles the mix of corners well. Predictable in changing conditions.
Power for the straight and strong braking into Turn 1. FR layout manageable in wet.
Nimble through corners but power deficit on the main straight hurts.

name: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
description: A benchmark Grand Prix circuit that tests every aspect of car and driver. Barcelona-Catalunya's mix of high-speed sweepers, heavy braking zones, and technical chicanes makes it the ultimate all-rounder test.

keyCorners.name: Turn 1 (Elf)
keyCorners.description: Hard braking from top speed into a right-hander. Late braking gains positions but lock-ups are costly.

keyCorners.name: Turn 3 (Renault)
keyCorners.description: Fast right-hand sweeper that rewards commitment and tests front-end grip under load.

keyCorners.name: Turn 5 (Seat)
keyCorners.description: Tricky chicane complex where a clean exit sets up the long run to Turn 7.

keyCorners.name: Turn 10 (La Caixa)
keyCorners.description: Hard braking into a tight right-hander. Key overtaking spot and easy to overdrive.

characteristics: Mix of high and low speed corners
